target.title: chore: address gollaw code health audit findings (#293)
target.body:
## Overview

Draft PR to track code health improvements identified by [gollaw](https://github.com/dovocoder/gollaw) static analysis.

Closes #293

## Problem

Gollaw v0.2.0-dev identified **760 findings** (health score 0/100, grade F) across 14 analyzers:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|------:|
| 🔴 Critical | 4 |
| 🟡 Warning | 501 |
| 🔵 Info | 182 |
| ⚪ Hint | 73 |

Top categories: deadcode (369), duplication (89), large-functions (83), thin-wrappers (69), churn (39), api-surface (38), complexity (35).

Full breakdown: see issue #293

## Planned changes

- [ ] Verify SQL injection false positives (3 critical — likely fmt.Sprintf in error messages, not SQL)
- [ ] Remove genuinely dead code (old migration functions, unused helpers)
- [ ] Refactor large functions (BackfillHistory 190L, storeParsedMessage 169L, Sync 155L, extractBusinessText 144L)
- [ ] Extract duplicated code patterns (delegated send IPC, poll resolution)
- [ ] Unexport internal types only used within their own package
- [ ] Reduce cyclomatic complexity in command constructors

## Notes

- ~340 of 369 deadcode findings are false positives from cobra's runtime command dispatch (AddCommand pattern)
- Most thin-wrapper findings are intentional adapters (sqlc, whatsmeow logger, lock syscalls)
- Platform-specific files (windows, darwin) show as unused when analyzed on linux
- Feature-flag and naming findings are low-priority/borderline

## Testing

All changes will pass the full gate: `pnpm format:check && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build && git diff --check`
